correctness.rationale: For each fixed odd m≥3, all maximal chords join the m cyclic vertex pairs. Both tangent-cone directional losses are strictly positive linear forms, with coefficients sin(π/(2m)) and sin(3π/(2m)); polygon cone Jacobian/area is exactly 2/m. Disjoint vertex corner point processes converge jointly to independent Poisson processes, and a uniform O(N^-1) expansion plus vertex localization gives the claimed N^1/2 weak limit with each vertex process reused in both directions. The bivariate joint survival is a Poisson void probability for two intersecting triangles; the shoelace area formula is verified. Each longest-diagonal deficit sum has small-t CDF λ² t⁴/6; overlaps involving at least three distinct vertex clouds are O(t⁶). This yields the stated m λ²/6 coefficient and correct parity comparison. The standalone checker executed 194 deterministic and seeded tests; experiments are only ancillary.

originality.rationale: The closest inspected primary full text, Wei Lao (2010), has area-uniform regular polygons only in the even-sided case (Theorem 6.8); its odd-sided chapter samples boundary points, which is a different process and scaling. Mayer–Molchanov (2006) explicitly report the unique-longest-chord hypothesis of Appel–Najim–Russo (2002), not met here. The positive joint survival correction uses the same vertex PPP twice and cannot follow from independent even-sided axes. Other studies of random interpoint distances treat ball-supported distributions or a single fixed pair. No equivalent odd-interior-area shared-endpoint law was found; residual historical risk is explicitly recorded.
residual_risks: The 2002 Appel–Najim–Russo article could not be read in full despite public searches and an unsuccessful lawful access attempt; its unique-chord hypothesis is reported by the inspected 2006 full text.
The claim could have an equivalent representation in less visible stochastic geometry or general polytope extreme-distance literature.
The side-count parity asymptotics are sequential limits; a coupled limit as side count and sample size increase is neither established nor asserted.

value.rationale: The odd regular polygon interior-sampling diameter problem is a missing natural parity half of an established family (Lao 2010), and shared diametral endpoints make the coupling genuinely different. A full explicit bivariate extreme-value law and m-fold finite representation solve the probabilistic dependence problem; the natural exact lower-tail coefficient and parity ratio 32/9 provide informative and non-arbitrary benchmarks. The theorem is not a special case of the independent-axis even theorem.
